record.original_question: Can the Boltzmann equation, or the Landau equation, develop implosion-type singularities analogous to the singularities studied for compressible Euler or compressible Navier-Stokes? The paper presents this as a plausible alternative to unconditional regularity and notes that such singularities would invalidate the universal hydrodynamic bounds.

evidence.quote: There are some recent results studying the stability of implosion singularities for the compressible Euler equation, and producing singularities for the compressible Navier-Stokes equation (see [77] and [78]). Can there be similar implosion singularities for the Boltzmann equation? The idea is to look for a solution that mostly flows toward a single point.
If such an implosion singularity was indeed possible for the Boltzmann and/or Landau equation, then the bounds (3.1), (3.2) and (3.3) would not be true in general.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the spatially inhomogeneous Boltzmann equation
  ∂_t F + v·∇_x F = Q(F,F),
and the Landau equation
  ∂_t F + v·∇_x F = Q_L(F,F),
for a nonnegative distribution function F = F(t,x,v) with (t,x,v) ∈ [0,T)×ℝ^3×ℝ^3, where Q is the standard Boltzmann collision operator (for hard or soft potentials, with or without angular cutoff) and Q_L is the Landau collision operator (e.g. for Coulombic or other potentials). For the compressible Euler and compressible Navier–Stokes equations, "implosion" singularities are known: smooth, finite-energy initial data leading to solutions whose mass and momentum concentrate toward a single spatial point, producing a finite-time blow-up of natural hydrodynamic quantities (density, velocity gradients, etc.).

Question: Do there exist smooth, rapidly decaying, finite-mass and finite-energy initial data F_0(x,v) ≥ 0 such that the corresponding solution F(t,x,v) of the Boltzmann equation, or of the Landau equation, develops an implosion-type singularity in finite time T* < ∞? Concretely, can one construct a solution for which the local hydrodynamic fields
  ρ(t,x) = ∫ F dv,  ρu(t,x) = ∫ v F dv,  ρe(t,x) = ∫ |v|^2 F dv,
and/or pointwise bounds on F, blow up as t → T* by virtue of the solution flowing predominantly toward a single point in physical space (analogously to the imploding self-similar profiles for compressible Euler/Navier–Stokes)? If such solutions exist, this would in particular violate universal a priori hydrodynamic bounds that would otherwise follow from unconditional regularity.
artifact.status_search_result: A partial negative result rules out certain approximately self-similar singularities for the Landau, Vlasov–Poisson–Landau, and Boltzmann equations, but no construction of implosion-type finite-time blow-up for the Boltzmann or Landau equation appears in the literature, and unconditional regularity remains open. The question of whether implosion singularities analogous to those for compressible Euler/Navier–Stokes can occur thus appears open.

status_evidence.title: Non-existence of some approximately self-similar singularities for the Landau, Vlasov-Poisson-Landau, and Boltzmann equations
status_evidence.snippet: Non-existence of some approximately self-similar singularities for the Landau, Vlasov-Poisson-Landau, and Boltzmann equations.
status_evidence.claim: Only specific classes of self-similar singularities have been ruled out; the general implosion-blow-up question remains open.

status_evidence.title: Well-posedness of the Boltzmann and Landau Equations in Critical Spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Critical-space well-posedness results for Boltzmann and Landau equations.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work focuses on critical well-posedness; no construction of implosion singularities is given.
